groups.sentence: Administrators maintain an inventory or registry of all AI tools and systems used at the institution.
AI systems undergo ethical review, risk analysis, impact assessment, and accuracy and robustness testing before adoption.
AI systems are evaluated and tested for bias and fairness before deployment.
Instructors select or develop AI tools that preserve usage data.
Faculty, staff and instructors monitor and validate AI tools and their outputs to ensure they work as intended.
Administrators continuously monitor AI system performance, accuracy and impact after deployment, and reassess systems periodically.
Administrators regularly audit AI systems for bias, fairness and discrimination, and correct problems found.
Administrators regularly audit and assess AI systems for performance, security, privacy and compliance with institutional policy.
Administrators maintain documentation such as model cards, approvals and records for AI systems, stored in approved repositories.
Administrators keep an audit trail and logs of AI inputs, outputs, decisions and agent actions, and retain records for audit.
Administrators keep AI data accurate and maintained, and AI systems transparent, auditable and aligned with public record laws.
Frameworks and standards such as NIST guide AI implementation, evaluation and monitoring.
